ERA V5 Session 8

What survives when a chunk ends?

The model carries one fixed-size summary vector into the next chunk. A small learned gate decides how much one token uses it; stop-gradient prevents training from stretching backward through the whole document.

Chunk 2 · the question arrives

Several paragraphs later…
What was the invoice number?
Waiting for the boundary.
Ask the question after crossing the boundary.
1. Write one summarym = final hidden state
It is one model-width vector, however many old chunks exist.
2. Cut the training graphm = stop_gradient(m)
The signal moves forward; gradients do not move backward across chunks.
3. Add a small nudgex′ = x + α · gate · m
Each token learns whether the old summary is useful.
Reported V4 scale: α starts near 0.078 and reaches about 0.391 by the 2B stage. With the default gate, the injected memory is about 6% of the current embedding magnitude—a nudge, not a replacement. This visual demonstrates the mechanism; it is not a trained retrieval benchmark.
